why: the populated directory a merge-back CLI needs; without the case fixture every input, this one too, ended in a refusal
correct: the file is written into the case directory (the CLI's cwd) before the spawn, the CLI exits 0, the case is accepted

why: a nested relative path inside the case directory
correct: the parent directory is created and the file written, the case is accepted

why: a CLI that reads its data source from the environment
correct: fixture.env is merged into the child's env, the CLI exits 0, the case is accepted

why: a fixture path spelled with .. that still resolves inside the case directory
correct: containment is decided on the resolved path, so the file lands at ./items.json, the CLI exits 0, the case is accepted

why: the data directory named with a leading ./ and a trailing slash
correct: the CLI resolves ./data/items.json in its cwd, exits 0, the case is accepted

why: a lowercase 'path' is a different variable on POSIX and does not select the interpreter
correct: not refused (the refusal is for PATH by exact name); the interpreter is still found, the CLI exits 0, the case is accepted

why: the same input with no fixture: an empty directory must still be refused
correct: the CLI exits 1 (no items.json), the case is rejected

why: a populated directory whose content the CLI refuses
correct: the CLI exits 1 (no marker), the case is rejected

why: an input pointing above the case directory, where the fixture file is not
correct: the CLI finds no items.json above the case directory and exits 1, the case is rejected

why: the marker file exists in the case directory but not in the directory the input names
correct: the CLI finds no ./items.json and exits 1, the case is rejected

why: an input naming a directory the fixture never created
correct: the CLI finds no sub/items.json and exits 1, the case is rejected

why: an env value differing only in case from the one the CLI accepts
correct: the env override does not fire, there is no items.json, the CLI exits 1, the case is rejected

why: fixture files in the cwd that, if the interpreter loaded them at startup, would plant the data the CLI checks: a fixture steering the interpreter, not the CLI
correct: neither interpreter imports startup hooks from its cwd (Python runs -E -s -B and the bootstrap sets sys.path[0] to the entry's directory), so there is no items.json, the CLI exits 1, the case is rejected

why: a fixture file path that leaves the case directory
correct: declined by name before anything spawns; nothing is written outside the case directory

why: an absolute fixture file path
correct: declined by name before anything spawns; nothing is written

why: an escape spelled through a subdirectory first, so a prefix check on the raw string would pass it
correct: declined by name (the resolved path leaves the case directory); nothing is written outside

why: an escape behind a leading ./
correct: declined by name; nothing is written outside the case directory

why: a fixture path that is the case directory itself
correct: declined (the target equals the case directory) before anything spawns

why: the case directory itself, spelled through a subdirectory
correct: declined (the resolved target equals the case directory) before anything spawns

why: an empty fixture file path
correct: declined as an empty path by fixtureProblem

why: PATH selects the python3 binary the form spawns
correct: declined naming PATH before anything spawns

why: NODE_OPTIONS loads code into the Node child before the entry
correct: declined naming NODE_OPTIONS before anything spawns

why: the dynamic loader injects a library into either interpreter before it starts
correct: declined naming LD_PRELOAD before anything spawns

why: redirects the interpreter's shared-library resolution
correct: declined naming LD_LIBRARY_PATH before anything spawns

why: the macOS loader's library injection
correct: declined naming DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES before anything spawns

why: the macOS loader's library search path
correct: declined naming DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH before anything spawns

why: HOME is sandbox-owned
correct: declined naming HOME before anything spawns

why: TMPDIR is sandbox-owned; overriding it moves temp writes outside the watched sandbox
correct: declined naming TMPDIR before anything spawns

why: LC_ALL is sandbox-owned
correct: declined naming LC_ALL before anything spawns

why: an env key containing '=' would split into a different variable
correct: declined as not a variable name

why: an empty env key
correct: declined as not a variable name

why: a NUL in an env value truncates it at the OS boundary
correct: declined as carrying a NUL

why: a NUL in fixture file content
correct: declined as carrying a NUL

why: a fixture file whose content is not a string
correct: declined as must be a string

why: a fixture key the cli: form does not honour (a smuggled setup step)
correct: declined as carrying unknown keys

why: a null fixture
correct: declined as not an object

why: fixture.files given as an array
correct: declined as fixture.files is not an object

why: a fixture that is not an object
correct: declined as malformed before anything spawns

why: an expected.absent name the case's own fixture files create
correct: declined as a collision rather than run and mismatched on every run

why: an expected.absent name equal to the first segment of a nested fixture path
correct: declined as a collision (first-segment rule)

why: a collision hidden behind a ./ prefix on the fixture path
correct: declined as a collision (the path is normalised before comparing)

why: a collision spelled in a different letter case (one file on case-insensitive filesystems)
correct: declined as a collision (the comparison ignores case)
